stem.en: What difference inside the two grains makes salt water conduct while sugar water does not?

text.en: Salt is made of ions, formed when electrons moved. Sugar is made of neutral molecules, whose atoms share electrons.
Salt is ionic and so it is a metal, and metals conduct electricity.
Sugar molecules are larger than ions, so they block the current in the water.
Water makes ions from salt but cannot make ions from sugar, because sugar is sweet.

explanation.en: Both grains dissolve completely, but only salt brings charged particles into the water. Option b is wrong because salt is not a metal: solid salt does not conduct at all. Option c is wrong because the water around the sugar has no moving charges to block. Option d is wrong because water does not make the ions: they were already in the dry crystal.

hints.en: A current needs charges that can move. Which grain brings charges into the water?
